inline_comments.comment: The function silently returns `undefined` — no output, no error — when the framework is not `@storybook/react-vite`. A user on Angular, Vue, Svelte, or any other supported framework will run `storybook ai init`, see a blank terminal, and have no idea why nothing happened. At minimum this should log an informative error (e.g., `'This command currently only supports @storybook/react-vite projects.'`). Ideally the guard should be removed entirely: the instructions in `prompt.ts` are largely renderer-agnostic and would be useful for other frameworks too.

`logger.log(`Detecting agent presence: ${detectAgent().name}`)` runs unconditionally on every `storybook init` invocation. Users who are not running via an AI agent will see output like `Detecting agent presence: Unknown` every time they init. This is debug/development code that was clearly not intended for production. It should either be removed or moved inside the `if (isAgent)` block.

`await import('../../cli-storybook/src/ai')` crosses a package boundary via a relative path into another package's source directory. This bypasses the published package interface, will silently break if `cli-storybook`'s internal file structure is reorganized, and makes the build and test dependency graph harder to reason about. `aiInit` should be exposed through `cli-storybook`'s public entry point and imported by package name (e.g., `await import('@storybook/cli-storybook')` or the appropriate workspace package identifier).

`std-env` is imported directly here but is not listed as a dependency in `create-storybook/package.json` — it only has `semver` and the `storybook` workspace package as runtime dependencies. This import relies on `std-env` being transitively hoisted through the workspace, which is fragile and can fail with strict package managers (pnpm, Yarn PnP). `std-env` should be added to `create-storybook`'s direct `dependencies`.

The `std-env` import (an external package) is placed after the relative local imports (`'../generators/types'`, `''../initiate'`), breaking conventional import grouping (external packages before local modules). It should be co-located with the other third-party import (`'commander'`) near the top of the file.

`import { aiInit } from '../ai'` is placed at the end of the local import block (after `'../sandbox'`), but `'ai'` sorts alphabetically before `'add'`. It should be the first import in the local `'../'` group, above `import { add } from '../add'`.

`framework`, `renderer`, and `builder` are typed as `string | null`, but in `index.ts` they are always assigned via `data.frameworkPackage ?? 'unknown'`, so they can never actually be `null` in any `ProjectInfo` instance. This forces all consuming code (e.g., `|| 'react'` in `prompt.ts`) to defensively guard against nulls that will never occur. Changing the type to `string` would make the invariant explicit and remove unnecessary null-handling at use sites.

The JSDoc says "Represents a skill category" and "Each skill provides..." — stale language from when the feature was called `skill`. It should be updated to describe `AiPrompt`, e.g., "Represents an AI prompt containing setup instructions for a specific Storybook workflow."

The generated example declares the preview file as `preview.ts` but the decorator body uses JSX syntax (`<ThemeProvider>`, `<MemoryRouter>`, `<Story />`). TypeScript rejects JSX in `.ts` files — the file must be `.tsx` (or the `"jsx"` compiler option must be set). An AI agent following these instructions literally will create a file that fails to compile. The comment should reference `preview.tsx`, or the decorator example should use `React.createElement` to avoid JSX entirely.

The `dedent` template will not remove the leading whitespace from the second line. `dedent` strips the *minimum* common indentation of all non-empty lines; since the first line (`Would you like...`) begins immediately after the backtick with zero leading spaces, the minimum is 0, and the second line retains its full source indentation (~6 spaces). The rendered prompt will display the second sentence visibly indented. Consider writing the full message as a single string literal, or starting the template on a new line so `dedent` can strip a consistent indent level.

general_comments.comment: The old `storybook skill` command is being removed and replaced by `storybook ai init` with no backward-compatibility alias or migration notice. Although `skill` previously had only a stub implementation, any users or internal tooling that had already started invoking `storybook skill` will silently get an "Invalid command" error after this change. The MIGRATION.md should document the rename, or a deprecated `skill` alias should be retained with a warning directing users to the new command.

In `code/lib/create-storybook/src/bin/run.ts`, `detectAgent()` is called twice: once unconditionally on line 126 and again inside the `if (isAgent)` block on line 131. The result should be captured once in a variable (`const agent = detectAgent()`) and reused, both to avoid redundant work and to make the relationship between the two log messages clearer.
